trust_decision.summary: Which binary runs for a helper command (pamusb-check, tmux, findmnt, logger, gnome-keyring-daemon, ...) is decided by the caller-controlled PATH instead of a fixed absolute path, both in the PAM module (root at auth time) and in the user/admin tools.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'pam_usb tools' and PATH manipulation; the bare `pamusb-check` auth gate in the tools/ shell script is the most obvious PATH-resolved command.

fix_sites.entry_point: PAM auth: pam_sm_authenticate -> pusb_local_login (src/pam.c:98, src/local.c:381) and pamusb-check CLI (src/pamusb-check.c:62); tmux branch only
fix_sites.module_kind: PAM module core (C library, runs as root at auth time)

fix_sites.entry_point: pamusb-keyring-unlock-gnome (autostart, no args) auth gate; also id/logger/stat/awk/pidof/kill/gnome-keyring-daemon at lines 31,95-125
pamusb-conf --reset-pads=user (findmnt bare); same commit also replaces hard-coded /home/%s at tools/pamusb-conf:359 with pwd home

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/tmux.c:107 (C PAM module, reached from src/local.c:381; advisory summary names only the 'tools')

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report talks about the user-facing 'tools'; the tmux popen lives in the PAM module's local-login check, only runs inside tmux, and sits next to already-absolute /usr/bin/w and /usr/bin/loginctl calls (src/tmux.c:177, src/local.c:240), so it looks already hardened.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Keyring password file must keep parsing the legacy quoted format UNLOCK_PASSWORD="..." written by the old installer, and pamusb-agent must keep honouring an admin-supplied --check path; a fix that rejects non-/usr/bin paths or rewrites the file format breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: shell script bare command names (sh tool: pamusb-check, id/whoami, logger, stat, awk, pidof, kill, gnome-keyring-daemon)
C popen command string built with snprintf (tmux)
Python subprocess argv list with bare argv[0] (findmnt)
hard-coded /home/<user> home path replaced by passwd lookup (tools/pamusb-conf:359)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: pamusb-pinentry auth gate runs bare 'pamusb-check' via PATH before releasing the stored GPG passphrase
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Separate GPG pinentry helper (different author/feature, Python), not named in the report; fallback app path is already validated as absolute at line 149, so it looks hardened.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file and language from landing point (tools/, Python vs sh)

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Install-time admin action usually run via sudo with secure_path; not an auth path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as previous route; also lines 78 and 100

O8_uncovered_routes.route: pamusb-agent runs configured lock/unlock commands through bare 'sh'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Commands are admin-configured, env is replaced by the filtered XML env (no PATH from caller), agent is a root daemon started with a system PATH; ChangeLog lists the later fix under a separate bugfix (#325).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: pamusb-keyring-unlock-gnome --install/--uninstall keep bare mkdir/chmod/rm/stty/cat even after the published fix
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Interactive one-off run by the user in their own shell; published fix left them bare too (fix.diff:412-426).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a loginctl/grep/awk popen pipeline where one stage is written bare instead of /usr/bin/...
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pipeline already chains five commands in one string; dropping a prefix on one stage is an easy maintainer slip and sits in the same root PAM path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second subprocess helper (e.g. lsblk/udisksctl for listing volumes) with a bare argv[0]
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: pamusb-conf already shells out for mount points; listing devices via a CLI instead of the UDisks binding is a plausible alternative path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a default 'check' falling back to bare 'pamusb-check' when /usr/bin/pamusb-check is missing
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Lines 195-198 already handle a missing check binary; a PATH fallback for /usr/local installs is a natural convenience.

O9_family: CWE-427 uncontrolled search path element (helper binary resolved via caller PATH)

O10_build.language: C (PAM module + pamusb-check) plus Python 3 and POSIX sh tools
O10_build.toolchain: make + gcc; libpam, libxml2, udisks2/glib (C); python3 with gi UDisks, dbus, python-dotenv (tools); cmocka and pytest for unit tests
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/c/tmux_test.c (cmocka, popen wrapped via --wrap), tests/unit/python/test_pamusb_conf.py, tests/unit/python/test_pamusb_pinentry.py; no keyring-unlock unit test at pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Prefix /usr/bin/ on pamusb-check in the keyring shell script (or export a fixed PATH at its top) and stop, missing the tmux popen in the C PAM module and the pinentry gate.
